source.title: Best Practices for Biorisk Evaluations on Open-Weight Bio-Foundation Models
source.authors: Boyi Wei; Zora Che; Nathaniel Li; Udari Madhushani Sehwag; J. Götting; S. Nedungadi; Julian Michael; Summer Yue; Dan Hendrycks; Peter Henderson; Zi-Fan Wang; Seth Donoughe; Mantas Mazeika

page_placements.theme: Robustness defenses and alternatives, and the limits of their robustness

record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery and latent knowledge after pretraining data filtering in a bio-foundation model, extending the recovery question to a different model domain and mitigation setting rather than testing the named LLM unlearning methods.
record.gate_note: The study tests pretraining data filtering, not gradient ascent, Who's Harry Potter, RMU, or another unlearning method. Its fine-tuning and probing results bear on recovery and latent knowledge. It does not test ablation, quantization, prompt-based recovery, or whether an unlearning method reaches near chance while preserving general ability. Stepwise values shown only in figures are not transcribed as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests pretraining data filtering in a bio-foundation model (Evo2-7B), not an LLM unlearning method. Its fine-tuning recovery and linear-probing results bear on B and on the latent-knowledge half of C, as a new-setting result (T3).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors say data filtering is not tamper-resistant in some settings and warn against relying on it alone. They also say they do not claim it is ineffective, and that the real-world threat is not established.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates pretraining data filtering and subsequent fine-tuning or linear probing in a bio-foundation model; it does not apply an LLM unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery depends on taxonomic distance: inter-species transfer reached the benign-sequence perplexity reference quickly, while inter-genus transfer was harder and was absent for the reported Orthoherpesviridae/Simplexvirus setting. Probe layer-selection criteria also define separate reported mutational-effect results.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-filtered Evo2-7B can regain eukaryotic-virus capability through fine-tuning on related taxa, and its hidden states carry mutational-effect and virulence signal under linear probing, without any unlearning method applied. Recovery depends on taxonomic distance: held-out species quickly reach benign-level perplexity, while held-out genera recover only partially or not at all.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining data filtering in a bio-foundation model does not make excluded capability tamper-resistant: related-sequence fine-tuning and linear probing can recover or reveal it.

record.problems: Only Evo 2 is evaluated. Virulence data cover Influenza A only, and the authors say results for other viral families are untested. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these outcomes. Some reported results are qualitative or summarized from figures, without exact values.
record.rows_left_out: Stepwise curves and distributions in Figures 2–4 are not entered as separate rows where the text gives no exact result for each step or condition; relevant explicit endpoint descriptions and values are recorded above.

untested.parts: No unlearning method is evaluated for near-chance accuracy, retained general ability, or resistance to attacks.
Fine-tuning on unrelated data or on a subset of forgotten facts is not tested; only related-taxon data are used. No LLM unlearning method is tested.
No activation-direction ablation. The probing results are on a data-filtered model, not one that went through an unlearning procedure.
No newer method claimed to be robust is tested.

record.verdict_notes: I give no version verdicts. The study is about pretraining data filtering, not unlearning, so its rows do not bear on B or C as defined. The record's draft labels for B and C are therefore dropped, and the rows are kept under fits_no_version. Uncertainty is not reported, and many values are only read from figures or text.

versions.untested_parts: No unlearning method is tested for near-chance targeted performance, retained general ability, or resistance to recovery attacks.
Does not test unrelated examples or a subset of forgotten facts as the fine-tuning data; it fine-tunes on related viral sequences. Does not test the named LLM unlearning methods.
No activation direction is ablated. The probing results concern data-filtered Evo2-7B, not a model subjected to an unlearning procedure.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

relation.reason: The study runs its own fine-tuning and probing experiments whose results bear on recovery (version B) and on latent knowledge persisting despite removal; it does not merely cite or assume the finding. Verdicts stay none because the removal procedure is data filtering, not unlearning.

tranche.reason: Own results in a new setting (a bio-foundation model whose hazardous data were filtered at pretraining): fine-tuning recovery of held-out taxa and linear probing of hidden states bear on whether data-level knowledge removal survives cheap fine-tuning. No unlearning recipe is run, so the bearing on version B is indirect but it is a result on the claim, not a tool use (T4) or a bare citation (T6).

source_check.notes: Shares five authors with an original (WMDP), and the intervention is pretraining data filtering in Evo2-7B, not an unlearning recipe, so treat every version-B link as indirect. R1-R4 are qualitative or figure-read: the text gives no perplexity numbers, and R4's 'over 2,000' means across a 50-2,000-step sweep. The paper is internally inconsistent on the probe split: main text and Table 5 give 5,600/1,400/148,505 (as recorded in R6/R7), Appendix A.3 describes 624 samples per dataset with 7,384 train and 1,868 test.

statements.correction: Evo2-7B, eukaryotic viral sequences excluded in pretraining, no unlearning recipe. Same-genus fine-tuning: held-out species perplexity reaches benign IMG/PR level within 50 steps (0.72 H100 GPU hours). Inter-genus: 1,000 steps cut held-out Gammapapillomavirus average perplexity about 20%, still above IMG/PR; Orthoherpesviridae/Simplexvirus no significant decrease up to 2,000 steps.
statements.problem: No number in the statement is attributed to this study, so nothing numeric is misreported, but the cited rows do not show the factor the statement names. R1-R4 vary taxonomic distance of the fine-tuning data (other species in the genus vs other genera in the family), never forget-subset vs retain vs unrelated data, and no unlearning method is involved: the capability was filtered out of pretraining, so there is no unlearned knowledge being restored.

statements.correction: Facts behind it: held-out species perplexity at benign IMG/PR level within 50 steps; mean |rho| 0.034 to 0.164 after 2,000 steps (called modest in absolute terms); base-model probe |rho| 0.159 (val-Spearman) and 0.151 (train-RMSE), comparable to ESM2-650M; virulence probe max Pearson 0.46, 77% over LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct. Inter-genus recovery partial (about 20%) or absent; fine-tuning adds only 5% to the virulence probe.
statements.problem: None. Every element is in the text: species-level recovery by fine-tuning on related taxa (R1, R2), fine-tuning gain on mutational effects (R5), and probes reading mutational-effect and virulence signal from hidden states (R6-R8). The statement limits itself to 'fine-tuning on related taxa' and asserts neither complete nor inter-genus recovery, matching the abstract's 'recovered in some cases'.

reader_labels.reason: Fine-tuning brought held-out species perplexity to the benign IMG/PR level within 50 steps and raised mean |ρ| from 0.034 to 0.164 (R1, R2, R5).

reader_labels.reason: Recovery across genera was incomplete or absent in the reported settings, and the virulence-probe gain after fine-tuning was marginal (R3, R4, R9).
